# Description

When XLA + TE/JAX's stream capture dry-run warmup + TE core CuTeDSL backend are all put together, we see `CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED` on some tests. Long-term, I am investigating further to make this compatible. But short-term, I will be disabling the TE core CuTeDSL backend in TE/JAX until we are compatible with this backend.

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes


# Checklist:

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

nodes.body:
Confidence Score: 4/5

**[Medium impact]** The change affects processes that import the JAX package\. The PR appears safe to merge, with a non-blocking concern that PyTorch-only users can lose their requested CuTeDSL backend.

Findings

1.  **PyTorch loses CuTeDSL** ▶

Summary

Disables the shared CuTeDSL backend when TE imports JAX. - JAX imports turn off the CuTeDSL backend setting. Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: ["\[JAX\] Disable CuTeDSL at import time"](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/e368c226bc558de18c0eb94138cc026de9d2fa50) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

**PyTorch loses CuTeDSL** If a PyTorch-only user has JAX installed but not the TE JAX extension, this assignment still disables their requested CuTeDSL backend. The parent package eagerly imports `transformer_engine.jax`. This code changes the environment before `load_framework_extension("jax")` fails, and the parent catches that failure without restoring the setting. PyTorch's first MXFP8 call then caches the disabled setting and falls back to regular CUDA kernels despite `NVTE_ENABLE_CUTEDSL_BACKEND=1`. Only disable the backend after confirming that the TE JAX extension is available. **Knowledge Base Used:** [CuTeDSL kernel backend](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/native-cutedsl.md)
